repo.name: LanternEngine
repo.description: Lantern Engine: run your own copy of Bloodborne on Windows. A launcher and engine where the game's code runs natively; bring your own game dump.

releases.name: Lantern Engine 0.9.39 beta 31
releases.body:
Pre-release: a beta for testing, expect rough edges.

## Native renderer: draws from the game's own objects

- Draws now come from the game's own graphics objects instead of being read back from its command buffers: each draw's bindings, render state, render targets, and vertex, index and resource buffers. This is the next big step toward Lantern's own renderer.
- **It's on by default in this beta.** If something draws wrong or the game crashes, turn off **Engine › Native renderer: draws** and tell us. Safe mode turns it off too.
- In our test runs, about 7.8 million draws matched the old path exactly, with 0 differences. 60% of buffer bindings now go straight through Lantern, and the slow buffer path is used half as often.
- Not a frame rate boost yet. This step moves the work to the native path, and the speed gains come in the next steps.

## Lighting fixes

- **Lamp fog no longer pops in and out** while the camera moves in areas with lots of lamps, like the Forbidden Woods bridge. Lamps are remembered and fade in and out smoothly. Engine › Graphics › "Steady lamp fog" turns it off. By @rhkim1292 ([#90](https://github.com/Awakenchan/LanternEngine/pull/90))
- **Volumetric sunlight no longer flickers to another colour.** The fog follows the area's own light and changes colour smoothly. Places that used to look steadily white may now look blue, which is the fix working. Engine › Graphics › "Steady sunlight color" turns it off. By @rhkim1292 ([#91](https://github.com/Awakenchan/LanternEngine/pull/91))

## Seamless co-op

- A guest now gets the map's treasure and chests in the host's world, with their own pickups.
- A guest gets their full enemy drops.
- NPCs no longer turn into ghosts for a guest.
- NPCs who talk through windows talk to a guest from the start and hand over their key items.

## Memory

- Fixed a video memory leak: reduced-size copies of images were kept after the image was gone. This mostly helps cards with 8 GB or less.

## Launcher

- **Saves:** each hunter now has its own tile with level, bosses, time played and last save, newest first.
- **Windows 11:** hover the maximize button for the snap layouts.
- **Settings › Appearance › Background › Windows Mica:** a see-through window tinted by your theme colour (Windows 11).
- The launcher asks once whether to use the settings this beta was tested with. Your own are saved, and Settings › Beta tested settings brings them back.

## Linux

- Ultrawide screens: the UI is centred and the menu movies are widened, as on Windows. By @Ndmjohansen ([#92](https://github.com/Awakenchan/LanternEngine/pull/92))

## From contributors

Thank you @rhkim1292 and @Ndmjohansen!

## Not tested yet

- Native draws were played on an RTX 5060 on Windows only. AMD, Intel, older NVIDIA cards and Linux haven't tried them. The last two native changes (the loading-stall fix and turning it on by default) haven't been played yet.
- The seamless co-op fixes haven't been played with two players yet.
- The memory leak fix hasn't been played yet.
- The lighting fixes were tested by their author on an RTX 3080 on Windows, not on AMD or Linux.
- This build wasn't test-booted before release, and the Vulkan validation run on a software driver wasn't done for this beta.

releases.name: Lantern Engine 0.9.39 beta 30
releases.body:
Pre-release: a beta for testing, expect rough edges.

## From contributors

Thank you!

- **Online: no more frame hitches when players connect or leave**, by @Ndmjohansen. ([#89](https://github.com/Awakenchan/LanternEngine/pull/89)) Every new peer (an invader, a summon, other players' signs and ghosts) froze the game for a server round trip, about 270 ms and up to 500 ms. Leaving a room after an invasion did the same. Both now happen beside the game.
- **4K menus: smooth filtering and mipmaps**, by @Ndmjohansen. ([#88](https://github.com/Awakenchan/LanternEngine/pull/88)) The game samples menu art texel by texel, so the 4K art looked blocky and shimmered. It's filtered properly now, the HUD uses its 4K art too, and the faint box around the HUD bars' glows is gone. Only when 4K menus are on.
  - Rebuild your 4K menus to get the 4K HUD. Until then the HUD uses the game's own art, cleaned and smoothed.
  - `BB_UI_SMOOTH=0` keeps the old sampling. `BB_UI_LOD_BIAS` sets the sharpness, from `0` (softest) to `-2` (sharpest), default `-0.5`.

## Beta tested settings

- The launcher asks once whether to use the settings this beta was tested with. Your own are saved, and Settings › Beta tested settings brings them back.

## Not tested yet

- This build wasn't test-booted here before release. Both changes were tested by their author on beta 29.
- The online change was tested by its author in an invasion and a host session on The Hunter's Dream. Seamless co-op rooms don't use this path.
- The 4K menu change was tested by its author at 3440x1440. Linux, AMD and Intel cards haven't tried it here. 4K menus now keep mipmaps, so they use about a third more video memory.

releases.name: Lantern Engine 0.9.39 beta 29
releases.body:
## Camera

- The camera follows as it did before beta 25. The frame-time smoothing added then made it feel too far behind at high frame rates, so it's off now. `LANTERN_CAMERA_TIMING=1` turns it back on.

## Seamless co-op

- Guests now get what a boss changes for the host, on every boss. The game skips part of each boss's script on a guest, so a guest missed the area flags it sets. Those are shared now, for all bosses.
- The story clock (the world's evening and night phases) is shared too. It wasn't before, so a guest could stay behind on rewards and changes that wait for it, such as the Hunter's Dream ones.
- Only what happens while you're in the host's world counts. A guest doesn't jump to a host's earlier progress.
- A guest's boss drop now waits until the game's prompts are back after the kill, so the item pop-up has a chance to show. The drop itself was already being given.

## Lighting

These are the optional lighting effects in the options. All numbers are from a test scene at 1080p on an RTX 5060, not from the game.

- Fixed: ambient occlusion (GTAO) and indirect light (GI) darkened open surfaces at glancing angles. With GTAO on, scenes will look brighter, closer to what the effect is meant to do.
- Fixed: volumetric sunlight could read the wrong shadow cascade at the edges.
- Soft sun shadows (PCSS) are about 3x faster, and with contact shadows also about 3x faster.
- Point light shadows are about 9x faster, and no longer break the render pass for every light tile.
- Fog around lamps is 1.8x faster.
- Volumetric sunlight is about 20% faster with much less dither noise.
- Contact shadows on their own are about 10% slower in the close-up test scene. Paired with PCSS they're much faster.

## Ray traced lighting (experimental)

- New option: Ray traced lighting. It's off by default and needs a restart to turn on. It traces sun shadows, lamp shadows and one bounce of light against the game's real geometry. It isn't a path tracer.
- It's heavy. On an RTX 5060 at 720p render with DLSS, one standing spot cost about 6 ms a frame. Early runs, before the last fixes, dropped to 31-38 FPS in the heaviest streets.
- Cards without Vulkan ray query keep the normal lighting, and the log says why.
- Known limits: lamp shadows have hard edges, cut-out shapes like leaves and grates don't block lamp or bounce rays, and the bounce only picks up colour from what's on screen.

## From contributors

Thank you!

- Brazilian Portuguese as a game language, without unlocking the region, by @Arturvitormb. ([#83](https://github.com/Awakenchan/LanternEngine/pull/83))
- Ultrawide: full-width menu backgrounds, dims and loading screens, by @Ndmjohansen. ([#85](https://github.com/Awakenchan/LanternEngine/pull/85))
- Intel XeSS Super Resolution code, by @frankzzz. ([#86](https://github.com/Awakenchan/LanternEngine/pull/86)) Intel's library isn't in this package yet, so choosing XeSS falls back to FSR 3.1 unless you add `libxess.dll` to `engine/xess` yourself.

## Not tested yet

- Everything above still needs playing in the game: the lighting changes, the shared boss flags and clock, and the pop-up. The pop-up fix comes from reading logs, so it may not be the whole story. The log now says whether the pop-up queued.
- A save that was already behind doesn't catch up by itself. It moves on with what happens while you're in the host's world.
- Ray tracing has only run on an RTX 5060 on Windows. Other cards and Linux haven't tried it, and frame rate on this build hasn't been measured in the heaviest streets.
- Linux, AMD, Intel and older NVIDIA cards weren't tried with the new lighting. The shaders only ran on an RTX 5060, plus a software renderer for the automated tests.
- Rooms that mix mods can still lose items for a guest. Everyone needs the same gameplay mods.

releases.name: Lantern Engine 0.9.39 beta 28
releases.body:
Pre-release for testing seamless co-op. Keep a backup of your saves, and send your log if something breaks.

The launcher asks once whether to use the settings this beta was tested with or keep your own. Your own are saved first, and Settings › Beta tested settings brings them back.

**Everyone has to update to play together.** The server now only lets beta 28 into rooms, so older betas are told to update. This keeps a room from mixing builds, which is why loot could go missing for some guests.

# Saves

- **The host's enemy scaling no longer sticks to a guest's save.** A guest who followed the host through a lamp or a load could end up with the host's New Game+ level as their own, so enemies stayed scaled when they played offline. A guest now keeps their own level.
  - A save that already picked up a host's level can't be fixed automatically, because the old level isn't stored anywhere. Use a backup from before if you have one.
- **Map scripts can no longer change a guest's NPC quest progress on arrival.** In beta 27, scripts starting up in the host's world could write NPC flags into a guest's own save. They now stay out for the first 20 seconds after a load.

# Seamless co-op

- **Faster summons in a room.** When a guest presses join, the host no longer has to press Summon: their bell rings by itself, unless they silenced it or a boss is up. Signs go up 0.5 seconds after the bell instead of 2, and the co-op menu rings sooner and retries every 3 seconds instead of 10.
- **Fix for guests getting sent back right after a summon.** A few seconds after arriving, a warp to the Hunter's Dream could fire and take the guest out of the session. For 30 seconds after a guest finishes loading, lamp travel is now blocked. If you really want to use a lamp in that time, do it again after that.
- **Fix for guests who never join.** A guest who started their game before the host was in the room could get invited forever without arriving. They now connect, and guests also reintroduce themselves each time they put up a sign.
- **Fix for staying dead after a boss.** Anyone at 0 HP for 12 seconds with no death step from the game now gets up where they fell. During a boss fight they still wait until the boss dies or the whole party falls.

# Save editor

- **Errors now show.** When Give or Save changes failed, the message disappeared straight away, so it looked like nothing happened. It now stays on screen.
- **Save changes works if the game saved in the meantime.** Your edits used to be refused if the game had changed the save since the page opened it. They're now applied to the newer save.
- **Each item you give now says so.** A row shows how many you added and reminds you to press Save changes at the top. Nothing goes into your save until you do.
- Changing an item's amount no longer fails after giving gear in the same session.
- Same on Windows and Linux.

# Not tested yet

- **None of this has been played.** It compiles and passes its automated tests, including a host and guest connecting through a local relay, but this build hasn't been started at all. Beta 27's loot, drops and NPC changes also still need checking.
- **The real cause of the warp back to the Dream isn't known yet.** The fix blocks it and logs which event tried. If you see `right after arriving was left out` in your log, please send it.
- **Staying dead after a boss:** the cause is likely but not proven. If you see `the game's death step never came` in your log, please send it.
- **Hardware and systems.** This beta only changes co-op code, not graphics, so the graphics checks weren't repeated. Linux, AMD, Intel and older NVIDIA cards weren't tried either.

releases.name: Lantern Engine 0.9.39 beta 27
releases.body:
Pre-release for testing seamless co-op with other people. Keep a backup of your saves, and send your log if something breaks.

The launcher asks once whether to use the settings this beta was tested with or keep your own. Your own are saved first, and Settings › Beta tested settings brings them back.

Everyone in a room should be on this beta.

# Seamless co-op: each hunter's own world

A guest now plays the host's world more like their own. Bosses, lamps, doors and story stay shared.

- **Guests get their own map loot.** A guest now sees items like the Hunter set, can pick them up, and keeps them in their own save. If the host already took an item, it's still there for the guest, and the other way round.
- **Enemy and NPC drops for guests.** A guest should now get their own drops, like the Blood Veil. This is the part we most need you to test.
- **NPC progress is separate.** Host and guest can both talk to NPCs during a session, and each hunter's quest steps go in their own save. The host's steps no longer get copied to guests.
- NPCs should no longer turn grey for a guest in the host's world.

Limits for now:

- An NPC is one character in the session, so killing or angering one does it for everyone in the room.
- Hunter's Dream NPCs work as before for a guest.
- A small number of items (about 186 of 7,193) still follow the host's world.

# Not tested yet

- **All of the above is untested in a real game.** It compiles and passes its automated tests, but nobody has played it yet, and this build hasn't been started at all.
- **Please check and report:**
  - Do guests see and keep map loot?
  - Do enemy drops appear for guests?
  - Does loot taken by one hunter stay for the other, including after a load?
  - Do NPCs talk, and does their progress stay separate after a reload?
- **Hardware and systems.** This beta only changes co-op code, not graphics, so the graphics checks weren't repeated. Linux, AMD, Intel and older NVIDIA cards weren't tried either.

releases.name: Lantern Engine 0.9.39 beta 26
releases.body:
Pre-release for testing. Keep a backup of your saves, and send your log if something breaks.

The launcher asks once whether to use the settings this beta was tested with or keep your own. Your own are saved first, and Settings › Beta tested settings brings them back.

# Seamless co-op on Linux (new)

- Seamless co-op now works on Linux, through the server or direct P2P, with the same Online page as on Windows: role, invite codes, plate names and titles, and open rooms. Linux and Windows players can play in the same room.

# Seamless co-op

- **Guests now see the host's world.** Before, a guest only got the host's flags for the map they joined on, so lamps were unlit, gates were shut, picked-up items were back and bosses were alive in other areas. The host now shares them, and guests stay up to date as the host plays. This only changes the guest's copy of the host's world, never their save.
- **The party follows the host's story travel.** The Cainhurst carriage, the warps to the Hunter's Nightmare and Byrgenwerth and the like used to be dropped for a host in a session, after their scene had already played. They now work, and guests follow. Hunter's Mark takes the party along too.
- **Guests wait for the host on the loading screen**, for up to a minute, so they arrive after the host instead of alone in the map.
- **A snatcher no longer takes a guest out of the session.** The guest lands beside the host instead of in the Hypogean Gaol. If the host is in another area, the guest stays where they are, still in the session.
- A guest's own pickups in the host's world stay picked up after a load. They don't reach the host or the guest's save.
- A guest's lamp request now shows the lamp's real name in the game's language.
- Following the host could put a guest at their old spot instead of the host's lamp. Fixed.
- A host who stayed in the lamp menu for over 2 minutes could lose the warp. The window is now 10 minutes.
- A session no longer ends when the host changes map, or when a member has no body yet right after a load.
- A party member standing on ground your game has unloaded no longer risks a crash.
- New lines on screen say when the host is travelling and when the party split on the way.
- One log message that could be written tens of thousands of times is now written at most once a minute.

# Saves

- **Fix for "stuck in the Hunter's Dream, can't interact with anything".** A save could hold a summoned guest's character type as the hunter's own. A save like that is now repaired when it loads, and the game can no longer write that type into a save.
- The bell can no longer be rung by a hunter who is still a summoned guest.

# Graphics

- A few cached shaders whose pipeline layout was invalid are no longer built at the start. They compile in play instead, which removes a crash risk on stricter drivers.

# Linux

- Now the same as Windows:
  - Setup guide
  - 4K menus
  - TOML patch files
  - Lamp2Lamp and the debug menu font
  - Hunter's Dream Mirror, Rebirth and PC Camera Controls switches on the Play page
  - Plate titles
  - Render scale, texture mip bias, DLSS auto exposure and DLSS sharper textures
  - AMD Anti-Lag 2
  - SuperMedo account page
  - Upscale before post-processing
  - The original follow camera at high frame rates
- Still Windows only: FSR 4 through AMD's Windows DLL and DLSS Frame Generation, because their runtimes are Windows only. Other editions of the game than CUSA03173 1.09 still start on Windows only.

# Not tested yet

- **Seamless co-op with two real players.** None of the new seamless changes have been played in a real session yet, on either system. Only automated host and guest tests over a local relay have run. Linux and Windows players in the same room hasn't been tried either.
- **Linux in-game.** The Linux build was only started on a software graphics driver for checks. It hasn't been played on a real GPU, and the Linux launcher hasn't been opened on a Linux desktop.
- **Real AMD, Intel and older NVIDIA cards.** Windows was only started on an RTX 5060, including with a GTX 10's and an RX 580's missing features simulated. The RX 580 run stopped after the first load.
- **The save repair on a real broken save.** The fix for being stuck in the Hunter's Dream hasn't been run on a save that actually has the problem. Keep a backup, and send your log if it doesn't help.
